To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

long-term treatment (28 days) with acylated apelin analogues ameliorates obesity and improves glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, lipid profile and respiratory parameters in high-fat fed male NIH Swiss mice.

long term treatment with apelin analogs (Lys8PAL)apelin13 amide and (GluPAL) apelin 13 amide, improved insulin sensitivity and reduced hyperglycemia in obese-diabetic mice and improved glucose tolerance.
Chronic treatment with apelin analogs ameliorates obesity and diabetes in high-fat fed Swiss NIH mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel peptide-based drugs to treat obesity and type-2 diabetes, and the identification of new targets for the treatment of these conditions.
the development of new therapeutic strategies in the treatment of type-2 diabetes and obesity.
the discovery and development of novel peptide drugs for the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the long-term treatment with apelin analogs (Lys8Epalapelin-13amide and particularly pGleu (Lys8Epapelin-13) amide) resulted in similar or even enhanced therapeutic responses to the GLP-1 analogue Liraglutide, in diet-induced obese-diabetic mice.

long-term treatment of obese-diabetic mice with acylated apelin analogues (L)apelin-12 or (L)aplin-13 amide improved insulin resistance and glucose homeostasis, reduced body weight and food intake, and improved lipid profile.
apelin analogues are a new class of antidiabetic drugs with potential for treatment of type 2 diabetes.

fatty acid modified apelins are more effective in the treatment of diabetes and dyslipidemia than liraglutile.
the long-acting fatty acid modified apelins are a novel approach for the treatment of obesity, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia and osteopenia.
the apelin analogues are effective at treating the metabolic syndrome and have a similar or enhanced therapeutic profile to the GLP-1 analogue, liraglutiide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the apelin analogues (L8Epal) and (L8Epaglu)pal ameliorated obesity and diabetes in high fat fed mice, and improved lipid profiles.

apelin analogues are effective in improving glucose and insulin metabolism, lipid metabolism, bone mineral density, fat deposits, GLP-1 and energy expenditure, which may be useful for treating diabetes and obesity.
